IS : 4086 - 1983

Indian Standard
SPECIFICATION FOR DISTRIBUTORS FOR SPARK IGNITION ENGINES

( First Revision )
0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 26 December 1983, after the draft finalized by the Automotive Electrical Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electrotechnical Division Council. 0.2 This standard was first issued in 1967. This revision has been undertaken to upgrade its contents and bring m line with international practice. 0.3 This standard covers the requirements and methods of tests for distributors for automotive application employing spark-ignition engine as the prime mover, with an electrical system having 6 V or 12 V dc supply. 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, with expressing the ,result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance The number of significant places retained in the rounded IS : 2-1960*. off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

TERMINOLOGY 2.0 For apply. 2.1 Distributor - Any device which incorporates a timing mechanism, a spark advance mechanism and a spark distribution mechanism all of which have a proper angular interrelationship in themselves. 2.2 Contact Gap - The measured minimum gap between the contacts of contact breaker assembly when the hea. is situated at the crest of the cam lobe. 2.3 Dwell Angle - The in degree for the duration the adjacent cam lobes. 2.4 Firing the adjacent angle of rotation of distributor of which the contacts remain measured shaft measured closed between between the purpose ofthis standard, the following definitions shall

2.5 Automatic Advance ( Centrifugal Advance ) - The automatic advance angle is the advance in timing of the spark measured in degrees between the spark at the initial set speed (the lowest speed at which there is no advance specified ) and the spark at the speed at which the required advance is specified. 2.6 Vacuum Advance - The vacuum advance angle is the advance in timing of the spark measured in degrees between the spark obtained at the `no vacuum' initial setting and the spark obtained at the specified advance is to be checked with the distributor Vacuum vacuum. revolving at a low speed when there is no automatic advance. 2.7 Type Tests - Tests carried These are intended specification. design of a given type of distributor. 2.8 Acceptance Tests - Tests lot for the purposeof acceptance 2.9 Routine requirements 3. 3.1 The materials used, and the design and workmanship in the construrtion of distributors shall be of such quality that will provide adequate protection, in the normal use, against mechanical and electrical failures and shall withstand the effects of changing weather conditions, water or excessive dampness, corrosion, dust, steam, oil, high temperature or any other influence to which they will be exposed under the conditions of their normal use. 4

NOTE - The use of the IS1 Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The IS1 Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirement-s of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by IS1 and operated by the producer. IS1 marked products are also continuously checked by IS1 for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions, under which a licence for the use of the IS1 Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.

5. TESTS

5.0 Conditions

for Tests

5.0.1 General - All routine tests shall be carried out with the distributor located in a suitable vertical housing and driven by a concentric driving member. The driving member shall be designed to drive the distributor shaft without imposing end loads on the shaft or side loads on the bearings. Shaft end float shall be restricted by a suitable collar fitted to the shaft.
Unless specified shall be 15 to 45�C. otherwise, the ambient temperature during the tests

5.0.2 Drive -- The speed of the mechanical drive shall be capable of being varied between 40 to 5 000 revlmin. A rotating spark gap synchronised with the drive shall be fitted, together with a graduated scale. 5.0.3 Instruments - Equipment shall be provided with meters for the measurement of speed, voltage capacitance power factor and insulation resistance. For peak voltage readings, the type of meter used shall be specified by the manufacturer of the distributor. 5

IS : 4086 - 1983 5.0.4 Low Tension supply and shall be maintained 12 volt systems. The supply shall be derived from batteries, 6.5 V for 6 volt systems and 12.5 V for

The earthed electrode shall be set to give a gap of in IS : 1062-19637. 10 mm with its axis in line with that of the high tension electrode. Rotary Spark Gap - A rotary spark gap set at 8 kV shall be for the visual detection of misfires at high distributor speeds. The spark gap shall be driven at a constant speed, preferably 500 revjmin. 5.0.7

5.2 Visual Examination - The distributors shall be checked for general workmanship and finish. It shall be free from any defect that may affect the function of distributors. 5.3 Dimensional dimensions against Check - The distributors shall be checked for the relevant specification supplied by manufacturer.

5.4 Test for Contact Breaker Gap or Dwell Period or Both The distributor manufacturer may specify either the contact breaker gap setting tolerance or the mean dwell period, or both. The measurements shall be taken in the following manner. 5.4.1 Contact Breaker Gap - An indicator gauge shall be attached rigidly to the distributor body with the moving member positioned centrally behind the moving comact. The moving member shall be so directed that it measures contact movement. The distributor shaft shall be rotated without side loading at any gap measured. The speed not exceeding 6 rev/min and the contact contact gap shall be within the limits specified by the manufacturer. in degrees shall be rigidly 5.4.2 Dwell Angle - A disc graduated attached to the distributor body, with a pointer over the disc rigidly A low wattage bulb of rated mounted on to the distributor shaft. voltage shall be connected in series with the contact breaker across the battery supply. The dwell angle shall be measured by manual rotation of the pointer at a uniform rate in the normal direction of rotation of The angle of rotation for which the series bulb is `ON' distributor. shall be considered the dwell angle. 5.5 Test for Firing Angle Spacing - The test set-up shall be as specified in 5.4.2. The point of firing, that is, the contact separation would be indicated by the series bulb. The angle contained between such adjacent break points shall be the firing angle. The firing angle spacing nominal firing angle. shall be such that it lies within f 1" of the

IS : 4086 - 1383 5.6 Slow Speed Test - The ignition coil and the distributor shall be provided with normal connections and each distributor plug shall be connected to a stationary three point spark gap. The distributor shall be run at 100 f 5 rev,`min for one minute, during which period there shall be no misfiring. 5.7 High Speed Test - With the connections as given in 5.6, and all the plug leads connected together to a rotary spark gap, the distributor shall be run at the speed specified by manufacturer as the maximum There shall be no speed for that type for a dur.ation of one minute. misfiring. 5.8 Centrifugal Advance Test - The centrifugal advance characteristic shall be within the tolerances specified by the manufacturer of the Characteristic shall normally be specified with speed distributor. decreasing from maximum, the zero setting having previously been made at a speed below 100 rev/min. 5.9 Vacuum Advance Test shall be within the tolerances The characteristics distributor. revjmin distributor speed and from maximum. The vacuum The vacuum advance characteristic specified by the manufacturer of the shall normally be specified at 100 with the applied vacuum steadily falling shall be measured by a manometer.

5.10 Insulation Resistance Test - The insulation resistance shall be measured between the low tension terminal of distributor and body, with the contact breaker contacts open and the capacitor isolated from the distributor, by the application of 500 V dc for one minute. The measured value of insulation resistance shall be not less than 20 Megohms. 5.11 Endurance Test

5.11.0 The purpose of this test is to assess the ability of the distributor to function normally under varying speed and vacuum conditions. 5.11.1 Equipment - The equipment is required speed cycle, with the distributor mounted vertically manner related to specific applications: 3 seconds Acceleration 4 seconds Declaration at 250 + 50 revjmin -0 150 rev,`min in 2 seconds to give the following and coupled in the

In addition to the above speed cycling, for distributors with vacuum advance mechanism, a vacuum cycle shall also be simultaneously applied to the distributor at the rate of 30 cycles per minute. RECOMMENDED B-l. LOT PLAN

B

OF SAMPLING

B-l.1 In a consignment, all the distributors of manufactured from the same material under similar duction shall be grouped together to constitute a lot.
B-l.2 The number of distributors to be selected depend upon the size of the lot and shall be in 1 and 2 of Table 1.

B-1.2.1 The distributors shall be selected from the lot at random. order to ensure the randomness of selection, procedure given IS : 4905-1968* may be followed.
B-2. NUMBER OF TESTS AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY

In in

B-2.1 All the distributors selected at random in accordance with co1 1 and 2 of Table 1 shall be subjected to all the acceptance tests except vibration test. A distributor failing to satisfy any of the acceptance tests shall be termed as defective. The lot shall be considered as conforming to the requirements of these acceptance tests if the number of defectives found in the sample is less than or equal to the corresponding acceptance number given in co1 3 of Table 1, otherwise the lot shall be rejected without further testing. B-2.2 The lot which has been found as conforming to the above acceptance tests shall further be tested for vibrations test. For the purpose the sample size shall be 3 for lots of size up to 1 000 and 5 A lot shall be considered as conforming to the requirements otherwise. of vibration test if no defective is found in the sample. B-2.3 A lot shall be considered as conforming acceptance tests if B-2.1 and B-2.3 are satisfied.
